dominant_strengths: Hero prism visual is striking — chromatic dispersion through the Vercel triangle gives strong brand-native visceral impact.
Customer logos rendered in their own wordmarks inline with copy creates a confident, editorial proof-point pattern.
Dark palette, mono-ish sans, and tight grid feel cohesively native to Vercel's established design language.
dominant_weaknesses: Right-column body copy is small, low-contrast gray, and visually orphaned from the larger left statement — hierarchy fights itself.
Tab pills (AI Apps / Web Apps / etc.) sit awkwardly disconnected from any visible content payload below, weakening behavioral clarity.
Lower card grid headers (Agents, AI Apps) repeat label language already used in tabs, creating taxonomic redundancy and reflective friction.
fix_priorities: Rebalance the two-column block: enlarge supporting paragraph or tighten left quote so they share an optical baseline and weight.
Tie tab selector to a visible preview/diff so the control implies state change rather than floating as decoration.
Differentiate section labels from tab labels to remove naming collision between AI Apps tab and AI Apps card.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leads via the prism hero, behavioral lags from ambiguous tabs, and reflective sits mid as the brand story is clear but not novel.
rationale.intent_fit: Solidly on-brief as a Vercel mid-scroll devtools marketing section — credible and brand-aligned, though not pushing the system forward.
